text:
A: Hiya, hun! Oh, look at you, you look so like my daughter did at your age. I'm Tracey.
B: Oh, haha, hiya. I'm Holly. Sorry, erm, is that a good thing?
A: It's a lovely thing! She's twenty-three now, Jade, lives in London, works in marketing. Where are you?
B: Stockport. Near Manchester.
A: Oh, I love Manchester, I've done a couple of hen dos there. I'm Chelmsford. So what do you do, are you at uni?
B: No, erm, I'm doing an apprenticeship. Lab technician. Quality control, so testing samples and stuff.
A: Oh, good for you. Honestly, I think that's so much smarter than uni. Jade's still paying hers off. You're earning, you're learning, nobody's handing you a bill at the end of it, yeah?
B: Yeah, that's kind of why I did it. Everyone from school's posting about freshers though, so sometimes I'm like, did I get it wrong?
A: No, babe. They'll be skint and hungover, you'll have money in the bank. Trust me. I left school at sixteen and went straight into recruitment, worked my way up to branch manager. You don't need a degree to do well.
B: That's actually really nice to hear. What do you do now?
A: Fitness instructor and PT. Spin, circuits, over-fifties strength. Do you do anything like that?
B: Erm, I go to a spin class on Thursdays with a girl from work. Well, I'm supposed to. I skip it, like, more than I go.
A: Ha! See, you need an instructor who'd chase you. If you were in my class I'd be texting you Thursday morning. "Where are you, Holly?"
B: Oh god, that'd be so stressful, haha.
A: It works though! I've got people who've been coming three years because they're more scared of me than the class. What music do they play at yours?
B: Erm, quite a lot of new stuff, like Sabrina Carpenter.
A: See, mine's all 80s and 90s. Whitney, a bit of Snap, some old dance stuff. The over-fifties go mental for it. The young ones look at me like I've lost it.
B: I like some older stuff. I nicked Arctic Monkeys off my mum.
A: Well, that's not old to me, hun. Oh, funny thing, my son's called Callum and there's a Callum in this as well, did you get him?
B: Yeah! He was really nice. He makes bowls and stuff.
A: My Callum can't make a bed, never mind a bowl. Seventeen, washing all over his floor. Do you live at home?
B: Yeah, with my mum and stepdad and my brother. And the dog. I pay board, but not much.
A: That's lovely. Do you get on with your mum?
B: Yeah, she's great. She's a physio. She'd probably like your classes, actually.
A: Well, tell her to look me up! Do you know what, if she's in the area...
B: She's in Stockport though, haha. It's quite far.
A: Oh, course, sorry, I forgot. Right, so what do you do for tea tonight, are you a cook or...
